slides.title: The MBA Entrepreneurship Model
slides.text:
The MBA Entrepreneurship Model
1
SCE 2026
Every student team is required to launch an Asset-light, High-margin, and Knowledge-based Business
Stages:
Stage 1: Form Team and Delegate operations Stage 2: Document business ideation meetings, metrics, and outcomes Stage 3: Create SOPs Stage 4: Acquire first customer Stage 5: Generate first revenue Stage 6: Increase revenue
Ideas to Select from:
1. Local B2B Micro-Consulting Agency
Many local small businesses (cafes, boutique retail, family-owned manufacturers) are brilliant at what they do, but struggle with digital transformation, inventory management, or basic financial forecasting.
The Service: Offer services like setting up automated inventory tracking, designing a local SEO, Google Maps strategy, or building cash-flow forecasting dashboards.
Build team specializing in: Marketing, HR, Finance, Operations and offer consulting to: Local businesses, NGOs, Small manufacturers
What You Learn Experientially:
o
B2B Sales & Pipeline Management: Cold-pitching owners and closing deals.
o
Scope Creep & Client Management: Learning how to manage expectations without working for free.
o
Value-Based Pricing: Moving away from hourly rates to pricing based on the ROI you deliver.
2. SME Digital Transformation
Help local businesses:
Digitize records
Implement CRM
Build dashboards
Use AI tools
3. "Zero-to-One" Skill Academy offering Weekend Bootcamps: Skill Marketplace

slides.title: 4. Corporate Training Startup
slides.text:
4. Corporate Training Startup
2
Students are often deficit in the practical skills that secure internships and placements—skills that MBA students should usually possess or actively perfect.
The Service: High-intensity, weekend bootcamps on specific, high-demand skills (e.g., AI, Stock Market Investing, Derivative Trading, Crypto Investing, Commodities investing, Advanced Excel & Financial Modeling, AI Prompt Engineering for Marketing, or Interview Preparation, Public Speaking).
What You Learn Experientially:
o
Product-Market Fit: Testing which topics actually get students to pull out their wallets.
o
Marketing & Customer Acquisition: Leveraging campus networks, social media, and scarcity tactics to fill seats.
o
Unit Economics: Calculating your exact cost per student vs. venue/software costs to optimize margins.
Conduct workshops on:
Excel
Power BI
AI Tools
Communication
Interview Skills
Sales Skills for:
Colleges
Schools
SMEs By arranging experts from amongst faculty or industry experts.
5. The "Middleman" Freelance Agency
Act as the agency owner and build a bridge between talented executioners and businesses that need work done.
The Service: Form an agency offering web development, graphic design, or content writing. Recruit skilled batchmates (e.g., computer science or design majors) as your freelancers, while you handle client acquisition, project management, and strategy.
What You Learn Experientially:
o
Organizational Behavior & HR: Managing, motivating, and retaining a team of peers who don't report to you corporate-style.
o
Quality Assurance & Operations: Ensuring the final deliverable meets client standards, even if you didn't build it.
o
Cash Flow Management: Managing the gap between when a client pays you and when you have to pay your freelancers.
6. Hyper-Local Niche Media Property

slides.title: 7. LinkedIn Branding & Career Growth Consultancy
slides.text:
7. LinkedIn Branding & Career Growth Consultancy
3
Building an audience is one of the most valuable business skills today. You can build a hyper-focused digital media brand around your university town or a specific industry niche.
The Service: A weekly email newsletter highlighting local business trends, student startup spotlights, or career insights. Once you hit 500–1,000 engaged subscribers, sell sponsorship slots to local businesses or corporate recruiters.
What You Learn Experientially:
o
Data Analytics: Tracking open rates, click-through rates (CTR), and subscriber churn to iterate on your content.
o
Media Monetization: Pitching sponsors, creating media kits, and understanding the cost-per-thousand (CPM) model.
o
Consistency & Operations: Setting up a content calendar and meeting strict deadlines week after week.
Business helps professionals, students, and entrepreneurs with:
LinkedIn profile optimization
Resume writing
Personal branding
Job search strategy
8. Industry Research & Business Intelligence Service
Offer:
Competitor analysis
Industry reports
Market mapping
Customer surveys to:
SMEs
Startups
Local businesses
9. AI Productivity Consultancy for SMEs
Many small businesses still don't know how to use AI. Business can help businesses implement:
ChatGPT
Claude
Gemini
AI-powered marketing
AI-powered customer support
